title: PROMOTION OF INDIAN CLASSICAL DANCES AMONGST STUDENTS
body_text:
The Government promotes the inclusion of Indian classical dances in school education in alignment with the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, which emphasizes art-integrated, experiential and multidisciplinary learning. The Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT), an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Culture, conducts training programmes for teachers and students of Government and Government-aided schools incorporating Indian classical and folk-dance traditions. In Madhya Pradesh, these programmes include dance forms such as Kathak, Rai, Matki, Karma and Grida. CCRT also has a Regional Centre at Damoh (Madhya Pradesh) for promoting local and regional art forms.
Further, the Sangeet Natak Akademi organizes the Kala Dharohar series comprising lectures, workshops and performances to promote Indian performing arts among school children.
The Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT) implements the Cultural Talent Search Scholarship Scheme (CTSS) for meritorious students in the age group of 10-14 years studying in recognized schools and children belonging to families practicing traditional performing arts. The Scheme provides specialized training in Indian classical dance and other cultural disciplines. Each scholarship holder receives ₹3,600 per annum along with reimbursement of tuition fees paid to the Guru/Teacher up to ₹9,000 per annum, subject to the Scheme guidelines. The scholarship is initially awarded for two years and is renewable based on satisfactory progress.
Under the CCRT Cultural Talent Search Scholarship (CTSS) Scheme, the number of scholarships awarded in Indian Classical Dance during the last five years across the country is as follows:
Year Number of Scholarships Awarded across the country under CTSS scheme 2021-22 225 2022-23 178 2023-24 289 2024-25 269 2025-26 313
Further, the Ministry of Culture also implements the Scholarships to Young Artists in Different Cultural Fields (SYA) Scheme under which scholarships of ₹5,000 per month are provided to young artists in the 18–25 years age group, including those specializing in Indian classical dance, for undergoing advanced training for a period of two years.
The Ministry of Culture promotes Indian classical dances among school students through its autonomous organizations, including CCRT, Sangeet Natak Akademi and Kalakshetra Foundation. The year-wise grants released to these organizations during the last five years are as under:

This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha today

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Culture informed the Lok Sabha about various schemes promoting Indian classical dance among school students, aligned with NEP 2020's art-integrated learning approach. Key initiatives include CCRT's teacher/student training programmes, Sangeet Natak Akademi's Kala Dharohar series, the Cultural Talent Search Scholarship Scheme (CTSS) for 10-14 year olds, and the Scholarships to Young Artists (SYA) Scheme for 18-25 year olds. Five-year data shows CTSS scholarships in classical dance ranging from 178 to 313 annually, with grants to cultural autonomous bodies rising from ₹106.94 crore (2021-22) to ₹150.61 crore (2025-26).
enrichment.context:
The National Education Policy 2020 marks a significant shift towards art-integrated and experiential pedagogy, moving away from rote learning, and mandates exposure to India's rich artistic and cultural heritage including classical dance forms like Kathak, Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya, as well as folk traditions. The Ministry of Culture operationalizes this through autonomous bodies like the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT), Sangeet Natak Akademi (the national academy for music, dance and drama), and Kalakshetra Foundation (a premier institution for Bharatanatyam and Carnatic music based in Chennai).

Scholarship schemes like CTSS and SYA serve a dual purpose: identifying and nurturing young talent while also providing socio-economic support to families of traditional performing artists, many of whom come from hereditary guru-shishya lineages facing economic precarity. Such schemes are part of India's broader soft-power and cultural diplomacy strategy, as classical arts are increasingly showcased internationally. The fluctuating grant figures and scholarship numbers also reflect budgetary allocation patterns within the Ministry of Culture, relevant to discussions on public investment in heritage preservation versus other developmental priorities.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Cultural Talent Search Scholarship Scheme (CTSS):
1. It is implemented by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
2. It targets children in the age group of 10-14 years.
3. It provides reimbursement of tuition fees up to ₹9,000 per annum.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, CTSS is implemented by CCRT (not Sangeet Natak Akademi), targets students aged 10-14 years, and provides tuition fee reimbursement up to ₹9,000 per annum along with an annual scholarship of ₹3,600. Hence statements 2 and 3 are correct, but statement 1 is incorrect.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Kala Dharohar' series, mentioned in context of promoting Indian performing arts among school children, is organized by which of the following?
options: Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT)
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that the Sangeet Natak Akademi organizes the Kala Dharohar series comprising lectures, workshops and performances to promote Indian performing arts among school children.

mains_questions.question: Discuss how the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020's emphasis on art-integrated and experiential learning can be leveraged to preserve India's classical and folk performing art traditions. Examine the role of institutions like CCRT and Sangeet Natak Akademi in this endeavour.
